title: Hungary at a Crossroads: LGBTQ Law Repeal and Drought-Driven Inflation Test… · 18 Sep
keywords: Hungary, LGBTQ rights, Orbán, EU law, inflation, drought, food prices, Hungarian central bank, European Commission, culture war, rule of law, Central Europe, EU politics, climate and inflation, Hungarian politics 2025
notes: Hungary's new government is moving to repeal Orbán-era restrictions on the "promotion" of homosexuality to minors, signaling a sharp break with its predecessor's social agenda and a potential realignment with European Union norms. Simultaneously, the country's central bank has warned that worsening drought and heatwaves could reignite food price inflation, threatening households already worn down by years of cost-of-living pressure. Together, the two developments expose the deepest fault lines in Hungarian politics: identity and affordability.
